Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The two umpires make their way out to the middle and they are followed by the players of West Indies. The skipper, Stafanie Taylor has her side in a huddle and offers a few words of encouragement. Alyssa Healy and Rachael Haynes are the openers for Australia Women. Spin right from the off as Hayley Matthews has been tossed the new ball.

Ian Smith inspected the playing area after the first innings. He informed that a heavy roller was used as chosen by Meg Lanning. He suggested that it will bring the track back the way it was at the start of the match. The Kiwi mentioned that there might be something in it for the pacers, near the good length area, the region Ellyse Perry benefitted from.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then! The task for Australia Women is a fairly simple one. They need 132 runs off 300 balls to register their fourth win of the competition and pull away a bit from the chasing pack. The Windies on the other hand need a bolt out of the blue to get over the line and go level on points with their opponents. It should be very comfortable for the Aussie batters but cricket can be a funny game at times. Join us for the chase in a bit.

Ellyse Perry (8-0-22-3) comes up for a quick chat. Smiles and says that it was nice to have a long spell and find the rhythm. Is happy with the start, to take wickets early on as West Indies are a very dangerous side. Tells that with the likes of Hayley Matthews, Stafanie Taylor and Deandra Dottin, there is a lot of firepower and it's very cool to take early wickets. Talks about the slope and feels that it creates a few opportunities as well but handling the wind is quite a challenge. She is very happy with the catching of her team and shares that they have been working very hard.

West Indies Women were the side in form but they seemed to have lost their way a bit in the last couple of matches. Last time, the middle order failed miserably and today the openers flopped. Thankfully for them, an out-of-form Stafanie Taylor did pick up the right match to muster up some runs and apart from her half-century, only Shemaine Campbelle scored some useful runs with the middle order performing poorly yet again. Their bowling has seen them through on a couple of occasions in the tournament but they have a daunting task ahead of them today and that too against a powerhouse batting side like Australia. The Windies will need a miracle along with a superb effort in the field to pull off an upset here.

Australia Women were off to a flying start as Ellyse Perry brought her A-game and knocked over the dangerous Hayley Matthews in her very first over. Perry then made it two in two and provided her team with the impetus that they were looking for at the start. Just when Dottin and Taylor were building a decent partnership, Perry got rid of Dottin before Powerplay 1 ended. For the next 10 overs or so, the Aussie bowlers couldn't pick up a wicket but then the introduction of Ashleigh Gardner worked wonders as she showed brilliant control and ended up with 3 wickets. Alana King and Jess Jonassen, the other two spinners, bowled well too as the latter ended with two wickets to her name and Megan Schutt picked up a wicket as well. Apart from Tahlia McGrath, everyone troubled the opposition batters and now it's up to the Aussie batters to chase down a small target and make it four wins in a row.

On a pitch that seems pretty good for batting, the Aussies have bundled out West Indies Women for a really cheap total of just 131 runs. It has been a top-class effort with the ball from the Women from Down Under and they are in command at the interval. As for the Windies, back-to-back underwhelming performances with the bat might cost them the game yet again.

OUT! Karishma Ramharack holes out! Tossed up, full and around off, Karishma heaves it away across the line but without much conviction. It flies to deep mid-wicket where Ashleigh Gardner takes a simple catch. Jess Jonassen finishes with a 2-fer as West Indies Women are bowled out for 131.
Commentary.Howout: c Ashleigh Gardner b Jess Jonassen

Commentary.Commentary: Loopy and full on off, defended back.
Full and around off, Shamilia Connell drags it off the inner half to deep backward square leg for a single.
Short and around off, pulled to deep square leg for a single.
Slight misfield. Fuller and around off, whipped towards mid-wicket where the fielder dived but failed to stop the ball cleanly. A single taken.
A low dipping full toss on off, it's pushed away from the toe end of her bat to short cover.
Full again, angling down, Karishma Ramharack tries to flick but misses. It brushes her pads and goes behind.
Chipped up! Full and around off, angling in, Karishma Ramharack lofts it over the infield at mid on for a brace.
Full and around off, pushed back towards the bowler.
Serves it on a length around off, Karishma Ramharack goes on the back foot and works it to short mid-wicket.
On a length and around off, pushed off the front foot to short cover.
Megan Schutt (8-2-21-1) is back on.
Too full and on off, Shamilia Connell defends it solidly off the front foot. A wicket maiden for Jess Jonassen!
Fullish and outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Arm ball around off, defended off the inner half to mid-wicket.
Gets forward to a full ball and dead-bats it near the surface.
Full and floated, around off, defended back.
Shamilia Connell is the last batter in for West Indies Women.

OUT! TIMBER! The 'round the wicket angle works for Jess Jonassen. She tricks the batter with a well-disguised arm ball. This one is served from wide of the crease, it lands on a fuller length around middle and skids off the surface. Shakera Selman shuffles across the stumps and plays all around it. Misses and the stumps are rattled.
Fuller and around off, driven through the line but straight to covers.
Wide! Fires one down the leg side, Karishma Ramharack tries to flick but misses. Alyssa Healy does well to stop the ball and also has a cheeky shy at the stumps at her end.
Flatter and on the pads, Shakera tickles it to short fine leg for one.
Flighted and around middle, Karishma Ramharack intentionally flicks it aerially over mid-wicket for one.
Loopy and full around off, it's defended back to the bowler.
On the pads, turned to square leg for a run.

Edged! Full and floated outside off, Selman outside-edges her attempted drive towards third man for a couple of runs. The umpire calls for one short run initially but then corrects her decision as Shakera Selman has done well there to plant her bat behind the crease. Good assistance from the third umpire there.
Short and outside off, played down from the crease to point.
Floated and on middle, helped to mid-wicket.
Fullish and around middle, Shakera Selman nudges it off the inner half to square leg for one.
Fires it full and on off, Shakera Selman plays a mistimed drive to covers.
Skidding down the leg side, Selman tries to flick but misses. It goes off her pads to the leg side.
Full and flighted on off, defended back to the bowler.
Tossed up on middle. Ramharack pushes it down to mid on.
Around off, kept out.
Floated, on middle. Ramharack eases it towards mid on.
Karishma Ramharack walks in next at number 10.

OUT! LBW! Fifty and out for Stafanie Taylor! Ashleigh Gardner is brought back into the attack and she gets the wicket the Aussies have been waiting for so long. This is nicely tossed up, on a full length and around off. Taylor doesn't pick up the length and hops onto the back foot. She looks to tuck it away but gets caught on the crease. The ball turns in and raps Taylor on the pads. The finger is raised but Taylor reviews. UltraEdge confirms there's no bat involved and Ball Tracking comes up with three reds. End of a solid knock from the skipper but West Indies Women needed more from her.

DRS time! Ashleigh Gardner has caught Stafanie Taylor in front of the wickets. The finger has gone up. The West Indian skipper has taken the review. Nothing on the UltraEdge and Ball Tracking shows three reds. With the glue of their batting gone, West Indies Women are now in danger of getting bowled out soon.
On off, pushed towards mid off.

Tossed up, wide of off. Stafanie Taylor drives it through covers for a couple of runs and gets to her fifty. What a brilliant captain's innings this has been from her, keeping her side in the match! She need to finish well though.
Ashleigh Gardner (8-1-17-2) is back on.

Fires it flat and around off, Shakera Selman walks across the stumps and helps it to short mid-wicket. Another tidy over. 60 balls left in the innings now, can West Indies Women get close to 175 at least?
Quicker arm ball on middle, defended on the leg side.
Skidding in from around off, Selman defends it from the inner edge to the leg side.
Flatter and on off, pushed away to covers.
Too full in length, around off, Stafanie Taylor drives it to the left of mid off. The fielder makes a fine stop and they get a single.
Flighted and full around off, defended back.
And again! Around middle and leg, Shakera Selman nudges it towards mid-wicket off the inside edge.
Sliding into middle, Selman flicks it to the leg side.
Around the top of off. Selman gets right behind the line of the ball to make the block.
Angling into middle, clipped away through mid-wicket for a single by Taylor.
Fullish delivery outside off. This is edged down to short third man.
Fuller and on middle, helped through mid-wicket for a couple.
Presses forward to a full ball in defense.

Great delivery. An arm ball outside off, Shakera Selman doesn't pick it. She gets forward to defend but it skids through and beats the inner half of her bat. Alyssa Healy has not collected it cleanly.
Flighted and around off, Shakera Selman defends it by getting on the front foot. It rolls towards mid-wicket, Selman looks for a run but Taylor has not moved an inch.
Walks forward and pushes it to mid off for a single.
Tossed up and around middle, Taylor forces it down the ground but the short mid-wicket fielder gets across to make the stop.
Full and flighted on middle, flicked in the gap at mid-wicket for a single.
Angling down the leg side, Taylor tries to flick but misses and it goes off her pads to square leg.
Shakera Selman is the new batter at the crease.

OUT! CAUGHT! Excellent running catch from Annabel Sutherland and Australia Women continue to impress in the field. Megan Schutt delivers it on a good length around middle, Aaliyah Alleyne turns inside the crease and attempts to work it on the leg side. She though closes the face of her bat too early. The ball loops in the air off the leading edge and flies in front of square on the leg side. Annabel Sutherland sprints across to her right from mid-wicket, keeps her eyes on the ground, covers a lot of ground and then stretches her body to complete a fine catch. Nelson has struck!
Commentary.Howout: c Annabel Sutherland b Megan Schutt

Commentary.Commentary: Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it back.
Pitches it up and around off, Aaliyah gets forward and pushes it to extra cover.
Fullish and on off, driven down the ground to mid off. Dot again.
A touch short in length around middle, Aaliyah Alleyne hangs back to punch but it takes the inner edge and strikes her on the pads before rolling away to covers.
Flighted and full, around off, it's pushed out with an angled ba to point.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries for Stafanie Taylor as she attempts to up the ante. Walks down the track to a full ball around off and powers it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Finds the gap this time. Short and on off, forced through covers for a run.
Keeps it short again, close to off, Aaliyah Alleyne steps back but again punches it to the cover fielder.
Short again, around off, Aaliyah Alleyne goes back to cut but it takes the outer half and rolls to short third man.
Flatter and shorter, on middle and leg, Aaliyah Alleyne goes back and punches it to covers.
FOUR! Clean hit! Pitched up, right in the slot and Stafanie Taylor just hangs back and thumps it right back over the bowler's head for a welcome boundary.
Full and straight, pushed towards mid on.
Pitched up, on off and skidding on. Taylor blocks it out.
Length this time, nipping back in a long way from well outside off. Stafanie Taylor stays watchful in her defense.
Very full and outside off. Taylor squeezes it out on the off side.
Pitched up, around off. Blocked.
Change in bowling. Meg Lanning has brought in pace from one end now. Megan Schutt returns. 0 for 14 in her 5 overs so far.
Full and wide, this is sliced away behind point by Aaliyah Alleyne for a couple of runs.
Sliding down leg, swept away towards fine leg for a run. The 100 is up for West Indies Women and it has been a real grind for them.
Fired in fuller, on off. Taylor jams it back to the bowler.
Curving in from outside of, full and on off. Taylor blocks it out.
On the pads again, Alleyne works it through square leg for one more.
Sliding down the leg side, tickled away fine for a single.
Slower through the air, full and on off. Alleyne keeps it out.
Around middle and leg, pushed out by Taylor.
Gardner comes 'round the wicket and drifts it down the leg side. Stafanie Taylor sweeps it fine to the left of fine leg and picks up a single.
On the leg stump line, Alleyne eases it down to long on for a single.
Angled into middle and leg, flicked away to mid-wicket.
A bit of an extra bounce on this occasion. Flatter delivery, around off. The ball takes off from a length and Alleyne is well beaten as she attempts to cut.
Around off, nudged away to short third man.
Floated up, full and wide of the off stump. Taylor defends it out with soft hands.
Full and on off. This is pushed towards mid off for a quick single.
Quicker one, angling into the off pole. Aaliyah Alleyne rocks back and cuts it to the fielder at point.
This is darted into middle. Alleyne presses forward to defend.
Jess Jonassen comes into the attack for the first time. What a luxury Australia Women have to bowl the number one bowler in this format at this stage!
Flatter delivery, on off. Alleyne cuts it towards point.
On off, pushed down to mid off.

Beaten! Lovely piece of bowling once again from Ashleigh Gardner. This is flighted nicely, around off and the ball just slides on across the right-hander. Taylor looks to block but gets beaten past the outside edge.
Tossed up, on middle. Stafanie Taylor strides out to defend.
On off, Taylor defends it under her eye line.
Flighted, around leg stump. Taylor misses the tuck.
Floated up, on a length and on off. Alleyne half-sweeps it down to deep square leg for a single.

Drinks! 30 overs have been completed and West Indies Women are barely going over 3 runs per over. The Aussie spinners have put a brake on the flow of runs completely and Ashleigh Gardner has been exceptional as she has picked up a couple of wickets. Alana King too has bowled well and Stafanie Taylor, the Windies skipper is playing a lone hand out there. She needs support from the other end and needs to face as many deliveries as possible in order to get her side to a respectable total.
Skidding down the leg side, swept to fine leg for two.
Full and around off, defended back off the inner half.
Drags it short, Aaliyah Alleyne top-edges her attempted slog-sweep and it drops in front of the deep backward square leg. They take a run.

NOT OUT! Tossed up, full and around leg, Taylor tries to sweep but doesn't collect. It goes off her pads to square leg and they decide to take a leg bye. Alyssa Healy races across to her left, collects the ball, turns and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end. They appeal, it's referred upstairs but Stafanie Taylor is safely in.
Run-Out appeal. There is a direct hit at the bowler's end and Alana King appeals. The decision is taken upstairs and the replays show that Stafanie Taylor was well in. NOT OUT!
Walks down the track to a low full toss and flicks it a bit uppishly but wide of short mid-wicket for two.
Quicker through the air, a bit short around off, Stafanie Taylor punches it from the back foot to covers.
Floated and full around off, drive back to the bowler. Maiden!
Flatter and on off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Tossed up and outside off, left alone.
Flighted and on off, defended.
Uppish but safe! Loopy and full outside off, Aaliyah Alleyne drives it in the air but it doesn't carry to the fielder at covers.
A touch short and outside off, Aaliyah Alleyne cuts but finds point.
Full and outside off, Taylor strokes with the spin but finds the cover fielder.
Floated and full outside off, it's driven through covers for a single.
Quicker and flatter on middle, skidding in, Aaliyah Alleyne goes on the back foot but gets an inside edge onto the pads in her defensive attempt.
Loopy and around off, Aaliyah Alleyne blocks it back safely.
Gets forward to a full ball and defends it back.
Turning away from outside off, played down to short third man.
Fuller and on off, driven to deep cover for a single.
Aaliyah Alleyne is in at number 8.

OUT! Run out, that's the last thing West Indies Women needed. Loopy and full around leg, it's swept wide of short fine leg by Stafanie Taylor and they decide to take the third run on the throw. Alana King fires it wide of the stumps at the striker's end but Alyssa Healy does well to immediately take the bails off by stretching to her right. They appeal and it's referred upstairs. The replays find that the dive has not saved Chinelle Henry. Just when it looked like West Indies Women were getting some control, they have lost a wicket.

Is that a Run-Out? Alyssa Healy whips off the bails and looks for the run-out at the opposite end as well but the batter at the other end is safe. The umpires do go upstairs for the original appeal and the replays show that Chinelle Henry is short of her crease even after putting in the dive. OUT is the decision on the big screen.
Fuller and on middle, blocked back to the bowler.
Tossed up, full and outside off, defended to the off side.
Flatter and quicker on off, Stafanie gets across the stumps and defends it on the leg side.
Gets forward and defends it back to the bowler.
Flighted and around off, defended.
Tucks it towards square leg for a single.

Direct hit could have been close. Henry drops it with gentle hands and scampers across to the other end. The fielder has a shy at the striker's end but misses. The keeper takes the bails off but Stafanie Taylor is safely in by then.
Around leg, helped towards short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Fine shot! Chinelle Henry has come out with positive intent. Loopy and full around middle, Chinelle Henry drives it down the ground, beats the bowler and mid on to find the fence.
Full and flighted on off, defended to covers.
Another slider, pushed through quicker and well outside off. Stafanie Taylor is beaten all ends up. West Indies Women are 77/5 at the halfway stage!

Was there any glove on that one? Flatter delivery, very close to the leg stump. Taylor shuffles as she looks to tickle it fine. Alyssa Healy fails to grab it and no wide is signalled. The replay shows that it came off the pads.
On the pads, nudged away behind square on the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Loose delivery and Chinelle Henry takes full advantage of it. Looped up, well outside off. Henry waits for it and thrashes it through extra cover for a welcome boundary.
Full and on off. Henry swats across the line but the ball goes nowhere.
Short and wide, enough time for Stafanie Taylor to rock back and ease it past point for a single.
Slower through the air this time and drifted onto the pads. Henry looks to work it away on the leg side but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Quicker and flatter, on off. Henry defends it out.
On off, blocked out.
Fuller in length and sliding onto the pads. Stafanie Taylor gets low and sweeps it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Alana King pulls out. Perhaps lost her run-up. Reload.
Around middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket.
Flatter delivery, drifting onto the pads. This is tucked away behind square on the leg side.
Chinelle Henry is the new batter.

OUT! BOWLED! What a ripper of a delivery from Ashleigh Gardner and she has two wickets in the over! This is bowled on a nagging length, full and around middle and off. Chedean Nation is drawn forward to defend and hence puts out a stride. The ball seems to be sliding across the off stump but just holds its line. Nation is beaten past the outside edge and the ball hits the top of off stump. With the off spinner bowling from 'round the wicket, Chedean Nation showed ordinary skills to not cover the line. West Indies Women are in dire straits at the moment.
Quicker delivery, fired into off. Chedean Nation manages to keep it out.
Full, on off. This is pushed towards mid off.
This one is slid across the right-hander. Nation gets beaten as she looks to drive it through covers.
Chedean Nation joins her skipper in the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT! Soft dismissal and Shemaine Campbelle has to depart now. Ashleigh Gardner tosses it up around leg, inviting the batter to come forward. Campbelle was looking to break the shackles and dances down the track to go after it. Ends up dragging it off the toe end of the bat and the ball goes straight towards Beth Mooney at short mid-wicket who takes a sharp catch. The fourth wicket is down now for West Indies Women.
Commentary.Howout: c Beth Mooney b Ashleigh Gardner

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker delivery, angled across the right-hander. Taylor hangs back and cuts it towards point for a single.
On a length, on off. Campbelle taps it towards cover.
Full and straight, pushed towards mid on.
Flatter, on off and skidding on. Campbelle plays it towards cover-point.

FOUR! Beautifully bowled but the ball runs away into the fence. This is nicely flighted, on leg stump. Shemaine Campbelle skips down the track and gets beaten in the flight. She gets a faint inside edge and the ball goes past the leg stump, into the fine leg fence. King cannot believe it.
On middle, played towards mid on.
Full, around off and pushed away towards covers.
Leg bye! Drifting onto the pads, Campbelle looks to tuck but misses. The ball goes off the pads towards short fine leg and the batters scamper through for a leg bye.
Flatter this time, angled across the right-hander. Campbelle hops on the back foot looking to cut but gets beaten past the outside edge.
Quicker delivery, full and on middle. Campbelle jams it out on the off side.
Shemaine Campbelle looks to take the aerial route but mistimes it badly. This is tossed up, around middle and Campbelle steps out and mistimes it towards mid on.
Around leg stump, pushed away towards mid on.
Flighted, around leg. Taylor knocks it 'round the corner for a single.
Floated and on off, Shemaine Campbelle tries defending but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It deflects away and Alyssa Healy collects the ball to her right. End of the over.
Flighted and on middle, Shemaine Campbelle goes on the back foot and defends it on the leg side.
No run.
A huge shout for LBW from Alana King and this time Meg Lanning does review it. The third umpire checks the replay and is satisfied that it definitely hit the bat first.

SAFE! A googly from King, landing it full and close to off, Campbelle leans forward to defend again near her pad. The Aussies think it has brushed the pad first and appeal. The umpire thinks it has come off the bat. The finger stays down. Meg Lanning opts for the DRS. The third umpire watches the replay and deems that there is no pad involved without having a look at the UltraEdge. Interesting. Meg Lanning is within her rights to register her disappointment.
Loopy and full, close to off, Shemaine Campbelle defends it close to her front pad. A muted appeal for an lbw, not given.
Tossed up, around off, defended to covers.
Short and on off, Campbelle gets back and cuts it in the gap at cover-point for one.
Flatter and on middle, blocked from the back foot.
Full and on off, defended to covers.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it back.
Short and around off, Campbelle pulls but finds short mid-wicket.
Flighted delivery, down the leg side, the batter fails to flick and Healy also fails to get across to it. The ball runs behind and they collect a couple. Given as runs.
Spin from both ends now as Ashleigh Gardner comes into the attack.
Full and on middle, Stafanie Taylor draws forward and blocks. A good start from the leggie.
Flighted around middle, spinning away a shade, Taylor defends from the back foot.
Short this time, around off, Stafanie Taylor cuts it close to her body but finds point.
Floated and full around off, Taylor drives it down to mid off.
Drags her length short and delivers it close to off, Shemaine Campbelle goes back and cuts it to deep cover for a run.
Good start from Alana King! Tossed up, around off and spinning away, Shemaine Campbelle gets back and offers no shot.
Ellyse Perry is finally given a break after bowling 8 overs on the trot. Alana King is now brought into the attack.
Full and on off, defended towards short mid-wicket.
Width outside off, Campbelle throws her bat at it and the ball flies off the outside edge. Goes to third man and they cross.
Around off, on a length and angling in, it's defended off the back foot to mid-wicket.
Hurls it on a length around off, slower one and it grips well. The ball bounces more than anticipated and strikes Campbelle on the splice of her bat.
Uses the angle of the bowler and works a length ball to mid-wicket.
Wide! Sliding down the leg side, Shemaine Campbelle fails to flick and Alyssa Healy is quick to take the bails off. Nothing doing.
Delivers it full and on middle, Taylor flicks it through backward square leg for a single.
Fullish and outside off, Shemaine drives but without much conviction to short cover. Just a boundary from the over.
Perry bowls it from wide of the crease and angles it in around off, Shemaine Campbelle defends this full ball back to the bowler.
On a good length around off, some extra lift off the surface, Shemaine Campbelle defends it with a loose bottom hand.
Bowls it in the zone outside off, on a fuller length, Campbelle lets it be.
In the channel outside off, Shemaine Campbelle allows it through to the keeper.
FOUR! Shot! Ellyse Perry is probably tiring. Serves it short and wide outside off, Shemaine Campbelle attacks it with all her might and slaps it to the deep point fence.
Ellyse Perry is into her 8th over now...
This is angled into middle and leg. Taylor flicks it leg side but can't get it in the gap. Just the single off it.
On off and there's a hint of away movement. Stafanie Taylor goes deep in her crease to push it out towards cover-point.
On off, Taylor nudges it out on the off side.
Length this time, close to the off pole. Campbelle plays it late and gets it down to third man for a single.
On off, firmly pushed towards covers.
This is pitched up around off and Campbelle drives it straight to the fielder at mid on.
Uppish but in the gap! Around off, Campbelle looks to drive away from the body and gets an outside edge. The ball goes past Mooney at gully and down to third man. They get a single.
Perry goes for the bouncer and bowls it over middle. Shemaine Campbelle somehow manages to get her head out of the way and ducks under it.
Full and outside off, on a driving length and this is hit straight to the fielder at the cover region.
Drop and run! Slightly fuller, on middle and leg. Taylor just nudges it on the leg side with soft hands and sets off for a quick single. The 50 also comes up for West Indies Women.
Length, close to the top of off. Taylor hangs back and pushes it away towards covers.
Leg bye! Perry angles it down the leg side. This clips the pads and runs towards fine leg for a leg bye.

Drinks break. Ellyse Perry has been on fire in the initial half of this game. Her three strikes have pegged back West Indies Women. She has hunted down the top three batters and has left the Caribbean team reeling. Stafanie Taylor is trying her best to revive the innings and let's see how things unfold in the middle phase.​ Ellyse Perry to bowl her 7th over on the trot...
Around off, this is nudged away towards cover-point by Taylor.
Ellyse Perry is exercising her bowling arm. Perhaps, signalling to her skipper that she can bowl one more in her ongoing spell. She has bowled 6 overs so far.

Another nervy moment but Stafanie Taylor makes it back in time. Tad shorter and outside off. Shemaine Campbelle cuts and cuts hard, through cover-point. The fielder gives chase and after a bit of hesitation, the batters do go for third. The throw comes in at the keeper's end and the bails are whipped off but Taylor is well in.
Pitched up, on off and blocked out again.
It's all dot balls at the moment and the Windies batters are getting bogged down. Full and straight, it's pushed back to the right of the bowler who makes a good stop.
Length, on off. Defended out solidly by Campbelle.
A touch fuller, angled into middle. Campbelle defends it off the front foot.
Length this time, around the top of off. Taylor defends it out on the off side.
A bumper now. It's well-directed over middle and Stafanie Taylor ducks under it.
On a good length, around off. Taylor nudges it towards cover-point.
On off, blocked out on the off side.

How did that miss the off stump? Ellyse Perry serves a length ball around off that nips back in off the pitch and does so very sharply. Stafanie Taylor makes the leave but it's a bit too close for comfort and the ball clips the top of the front pad and goes over the off stump. Meg Lanning consults her bowler and then decides against the review.
Good-length ball, on off. Campbelle hangs back and edges it down to third man with soft hands for a single.
On the pads and Campbelle nudges it through square leg for one more.
Around off, tapped away towards covers for a quick single.
Uppish but safe! A full toss, around leg. Taylor looks to turn it leg side but closes the face of the bat early. The ball goes off the leading edge and clears mid-wicket. Two taken.
FOUR! Overpitched and punished! Around middle, Stafanie Taylor with a gentle punch back past the bowler and the ball races away into the long on fence.
Fullish ball, on the leg stump. Stafanie Taylor works it through square leg and comes back for the second with ease.
Right on the money from the very first ball. Pitched up, on off. Taylor stays solid in defense.

The umpire signals the start of Powerplay 2! The fielding side can now have as many as 4 fielders outside the 25-yard circle till the 40th over. Also, here comes the first bowling change. Tahlia McGrath is into the attack now.
Outside off, left alone. End of Powerplay 1 and Australia Women have ruled the roost thus far.
Shemaine Campbelle is in at number 5 for West Indies Women.

OUT! CAUGHT! Third wicket inside Powerplay 1 for Australia Women and Ellyse Perry and it's the big fish, Deandra Dottin, walking back to the pavilion. What a terrific catch from Meg Lanning! Dottin had played out quite a few dot balls and the pressure was building. As soon as she spots some width outside off, she decides to throw her bat at it. Deandra Dottin though fails to middle her shot and it flies quickly to first slip off a thick outside edge. Alyssa Healy did react to her right but quickly pulls out. Credit to Meg Lanning for not getting put off there as she keeps her eyes on the ball, stretches to her left and snaps it with great reflexes. West Indies Women are in a big spot of bother now.
Commentary.Howout: c Meg Lanning b Ellyse Perry

Commentary.Commentary: Perry goes wide of the crease and delivers it on a length around middle, Deandra Dottin stands back inside the crease and defends.
Fuller in length and on middle, Stafanie Taylor flicks it in the gap, acres of space there at deep mid-wicket, and she collects three runs.
Beaten! Ellyse Perry lands it on a length outside off, getting it to straighten off the seam, Stafanie Taylor flirts inside the line with an angled bat and gets beaten.
Outside off, on a length, played with an angled bat to point.
Another slower one. Slightly short and outside off, coming slowly off the deck, Deandra Dottin goes on the back foot and plays it down defensively to covers. Maiden!
Lands it on a length and outside off, slower one, the batter mistimes her back foot punch to extra cover.
Stays on the back foot to a good-length delivery and defends it on the leg side.
Fullish and on off, defended to the off side.

Extra bounce from a good length around off, it's served from wide of the crease, Deandra Dottin gets cramped up for room and tries to defend it at the last moment by going on the back foot. It takes the inner half of her bat and strikes her on the pads.
Lands it on a fuller length around off, Deandra Dottin pushes it away towards extra cover.
Ellyse Perry pitches it up and outside off, the ball holds its line, Stafanie Taylor shoulders arms.
Full in length and angling in around off, Stafanie Taylor defends it close to her body.
Gets forward to a length ball and pushes it defensively to cover-point.
Back of a length outside off, shaping away, Taylor leaves.
Short and on off, pulled awkwardly down to deep backward square leg for a run.
Serves it on a length around off, Dottin pushes it from the back foot to covers.
Pushes a full ball with gentle hands to covers and steals a single.
A touch short and outside off, pushed off the back foot to point.
Uses the angle of the bowler and defends it towards mid-wicket.
Length and around off, blocked.
Angling in from middle and leg, Stafanie Taylor tucks it behind square leg for one.
Fuller and on middle, knocked down to long on for a run.
In the zone outside off, Stafanie Taylor shoulders arms.

MISSING LEG! Another escape for a West Indian batter, this time for Taylor. A corker of a yorker, dipping in at the right moment as it approaches the batter. Taylor tries her best to dig it out but is late in bringing her bat down. Fails to dig it out and is struck on the back leg. They appeal and the finger has gone up. Stafanie Taylor takes the DRS but is nervous. She now starts to walk after seeing the initial replays on the giant screen but then gets a big sigh of relief after watching the ball missing the leg stump on the Ball Tracking. The movement has saved the West Indian skipper.

Another LBW appeal and the finger is raised yet again. Stafanie Taylor has gone upstairs but unless she has hit it, she might be in big trouble here. UltraEdge shows that there's no bat involved and Taylor seems to be going off. However, Ball Tracking shows that the ball was doing a bit too much and going down leg.
Wide! Angling down the leg side, no movement there, Taylor tries to flick but misses.
Some swing in the air, landing full and close to off, Stafanie Taylor gets forward and defends it near her front pad.
Fuller again, around middle, pushed back to the bowler.

Jess Jonassen saves a certain boundary. Fuller and outside off, Deandra Dottin drills her drive through the line but Jess Jonassen dives across to her left to stop the racing ball at mid off. Saves three runs.
Delivers it on a good length around off, Stafanie Taylor taps it down to point and rushes across for a single. There is a direct hit at the striker's end but Deandra Dottin is safely in.
Good-length ball, around off. Dottin looks to punch it off the back foot but gets beaten past the outside edge.
FOUR! No fine leg in place and Deandra Dottin takes full advantage of it. On the pads, flicked away past backward square leg for a welcome boundary.
Full and straight, pushed back to the bowler.

NOT OUT! Lucky escape for Deandra Dottin and the West Indies Women bench is very much relieved. Megan Schutt errs in her length and serves a full toss that curves back in the air from well outside off. Dottin goes deep in her crease to club it away but misses the ball. She gets rapped on the pads and the Aussies appeal. The finger is raised but it is reviewed. UltraEdge confirms that there was a slight feather on it and Dottin survives.

DRS time! A big moment in the match as Deandra Dottin has been adjudged lbw after she missed a full toss. Looks close to the naked eye. Hang on, there is a SPIKE on the UltraEdge and Deandra Dottin survives.
On a good length, over middle. Dottin moves past the off stump and dabs it towards square leg.
On a nagging length, outside off and jagging back in sharply. Dottin hangs back and taps it towards short cover.
On off, solidly defended off the front foot by Stafanie Taylor.
Full, in that channel around off and nipping back in late. Taylor makes the leave and the ball dies on its way to the keeper.
Around the top of off, pushed out towards covers for a run.
FOUR LEG BYES! A length ball, sliding onto the pads. Deandra Dottin looks to tickle it fine but the ball comes off the pads and races away into the fine leg fence.
Good running! On middle, flicked to mid-wicket for a quick single by Taylor.
Beautifully bowled! Full, on middle and shaping away. Dottin looks to keep it out but gets an outside edge which flies past the diving fielder at first slip and down to third man. Single taken.
Full and angling at the toes. Dottin clips it uppishly through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Here comes the first boundary of the match and it's a genuine swat from Deandra Dottin. This is bowled in the slot, Dottin swings her arms freely and muscles it over mid on for a boundary.
On middle, pushed away to mid on.
Pitched up, around off and shaping in. Dottin looks to drive it through covers but gets it off the inner half of the bat towards mid on.
This is fuller and curves back in from well outside off. Dottin drives it firmly but straight towards mid off.
Sliding down the leg side, Taylor nudges it towards short fine leg for a single.
End of an eventful first over from Ellyse Perry, 5 runs and a couple of wickets off it. This is angled into middle, Dottin blocks it out towards short mid-wicket.
Good-length ball, over off. There's a bit of an extra bounce on offer and Dottin gets squared up as she keeps it down on the off side.

Perry looks for a yorker but serves a friendly full toss, on middle and leg. Stafanie Taylor clips it past square leg and Megan Schutt does well to run around from the fine leg fence to cut it off. The batters do come back for the third as well, good running.
Skipper Stafanie Taylor walks in next and she will be facing the hat-trick ball. Two slips in place...

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Ellyse Perry spitting fire at the moment and she's picked up two in two! Perry pitches this one up in the off stump channel at 109 kph and Kycia Knight looks to play at it with a straight bat. This time the ball seams away after pitching and takes the outside edge of Knight's blade. Alyssa Healy takes the simplest of catches behind the stumps and Knight departs for a golden duck. Perry will be on a hat-trick as well and she is just showing her class.
Commentary.Howout: c Alyssa Healy b Ellyse Perry

Commentary.Commentary: OUT! Cleaned up! Ellyse Perry with a gem of a delivery and Hayley Matthews is left dumbfounded! It is a perfect delivery from Perry. She bowls it on a length, angling it into middle and off at 112 kph. The ball straightens ever so slightly after pitching and Matthews misses the defensive block. The ball goes past the outside edge and hits the top of off. The in-form Matthews departs for a duck and Australia Women have a dream start here.
Early exit for Hayley Matthews and that has brought Kycia Knight to the crease in the second over itself.
WIDE! And again! This time sliding down the leg side with the angle.
WIDE! Perry looks to shape it away from the leg stump but spills it down the leg side. Wide signalled.
Pitched up, around off and shaping away nicely. Matthews plays it with the swing and towards covers.
Ellyse Perry to run in from the opposite end. A slip and gully in place...

Leg bye! Length again, around off and swinging back in a long way. Hayley Matthews shuffles across the stumps but misses the flick. The ball goes off the pads towards short fine leg. They get the leg bye. Just 2 runs off the first over.
On a length, angling into the pads. Matthews tucks it away on the leg side.
Schutt goes wide of the crease and bowls it on the pads. Deandra Dottin pushes it through mid-wicket and picks up a single West Indies Women are now underway.
Another big inswinging delivery. This one starts on off and ends up crashing into the pads beyond the leg stump.
Pitched up, on off. This is pushed back towards the bowler.
Schutt starts off with a big in-dipper. This is full and curves back in a long way from around off and ends at Dottin's toes. The ball hits the boot and goes onto the off side.

Done with all the pre-match formalities and it's now time to get underway. Despite a delay of 30 minutes, the good thing is that we have not lost a single over. The Aussie girls get into a huddle before spreading on the field. Deandra Dottin and Hayley Matthews, the power couple of West Indies Women batting, walk out to open the innings. They were on fire against India Women and would love to repeat the same here. Megan Schutt, as expected, will take the first new ball. A wide slip in place along with a catcher at short mid-wicket. Here we go...

The overcast conditions take a break, at least for now, as the sun is peeping out from the clouds. The players from both groups come out to the middle and as has been the tradition, they will first line up for the national anthems. Rally 'Round The West Indies followed by Advance Australia Fair...

Meg Lanning, the captain of Australia Women, says that bowling first is not too bad in these conditions. She is not expecting any more rain. Informs about a couple of changes in the XI - Jess Jonassen and Annabel Sutherland are featuring in place of Darcie Brown and Amanda-Jade Wellington, and it's due to the conditions and the match-ups. Adds that they have bowled very well in the tournament so far. She is looking forward to the challenge of bowling to the batters of the West Indies.

West Indies Women skipper Stafanie Taylor says that it's a good wicket and runs on board are always crucial and they have defended well so far. About Dottin, she mentions that she is fit and will play today but not sure if she's going to bowl. Informs that Anisa misses out and Karishma Ramharack comes in and it's not because of form but because of match-ups. Adds that they learnt a lot from the India game and will look to execute their plans better today.

West Indies Women (Playing XI) - Deandra Dottin, Hayley Matthews, Kycia Knight, Stafanie Taylor (C), Shemaine Campbelle (WK), Chedean Nation, Chinelle Henry, Aaliyah Alleyne, Shakera Selman, Karishma Ramharack (In for Anisa Mohammed), Shamilia Connell.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Rachael Haynes, Alyssa Healy (WK), Meg Lanning (C), Ellyse Perry, Beth Mooney, Tahlia McGrath, Ashleigh Gardner, Annabel Sutherland (In for Darcie Brown), Jess Jonassen (In for Amanda-Jade Wellington), Alana King and Megan Schutt.
TOSS - Up goes the flip of the coin and it lands in favour of West Indies Women. They have elected to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Craig McMillan is pitchside and mentions that there's been a bit of rain around and the conditions are still overcast. He adds that the ground is a big one and the spinners will come into play. Debbie Hockley joins him and mentions that the pitch will stay true but given the overhead conditions, the team winning the toss might look to bat second. She also mentions that the average bounce on this ground is higher than all other venues and the spinners also get good bounce.

UPDATE - 3.05 am IST (9.35 pm GMT, the previous day) - There's been a bit of rain around this morning and a slight drizzle is still going on. The good news is that the covers are off and the Toss will now take place at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, the previous day) with the match to start 30 minutes after that.

After a sensational start to the tournament by winning two matches on the trot, that too against sides like New Zealand and England, West Indies Women were handed a thumping defeat at the hands of India in their previous match and will look to bounce back against the mighty Aussies which won't be easy but not impossible either. So, will the Aussies blow the Windies out of the water? Or will the Windies take out another big gun? We'll find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

Australia Women are the favourites to win the World Cup and after a narrow victory over arch-rivals England, the Aussies absolutely demolished their Trans-Tasmanian rivals and hosts New Zealand in the previous game, having comfortably won against Pakistan in the match before that as well. A return to form for Ellyse Perry and the sensational return made by Ashleigh Gardner means that they are now stronger than ever and will look to make it four wins out of four and pull away from the chasing pack.

The 2022 edition of the Women's World Cup is moving along at a brisk pace and in match number 14, Australia Women take on West Indies Women. A match that seems to provide a lot of entertainment as both teams look to get another win and the Windies will look to go level on points with their opponents. On that note, welcome to the coverage.
... MATCH DAY ...
